name: Northwind Robotics handbook (synthetic)
description: A fictional 12-page company handbook written for this evaluation. Each question has exactly one gold page and a short answer string used for LLM answer checks.

pages.text: Welcome to Northwind Robotics. Northwind Robotics was founded in 2011 by Priya Raman and Tomas Keller in a rented garage in Tampere, Finland. The company designs autonomous warehouse robots, most notably the Hauler series, and today employs roughly 640 people across three sites. Our mission is to remove repetitive lifting from human work. This handbook describes how we work, the benefits available to staff, and the key specifications of our products. It is reviewed every January by the People Operations team, and the version you are reading is revision 14. If anything in this handbook conflicts with your employment contract, the contract takes precedence. Questions about the handbook itself should be sent to the People Operations mailbox rather than to your manager.

Working hours and remote work. Standard working time is 37.5 hours per week. Core collaboration hours are 10:00 to 15:00 local time, during which employees are expected to be reachable. Outside core hours, schedules are flexible and agreed with your team lead. Employees may work remotely up to three days per week; engineering roles that require lab access must be on site at least two days per week. Fully remote arrangements require approval from a department director and are reviewed every six months. Overtime must be pre-approved in the HR portal and is compensated either at 150 percent pay or as time off in lieu, at the employee's choice. Night work in the robot test hall between 22:00 and 06:00 is not permitted without a second person present.

Holidays and leave. Full-time employees receive 27 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, in addition to public holidays. Unused leave up to a maximum of 5 days may be carried over into the following year and must be used by the end of March. Parental leave is paid at full salary for the first 16 weeks for all parents regardless of gender. Sick leave requires a doctor's note only after the fourth consecutive day of absence. Employees also receive one volunteering day per year to support a registered charity of their choice. Leave requests should be submitted at least two weeks in advance through the HR portal, except for sick leave and bereavement leave, which can be recorded retroactively.

Compensation and benefits. Salaries are reviewed once a year in April, based on a published salary band framework with eight levels, L1 through L8. Every employee is eligible for the annual profit sharing bonus, which is capped at 12 percent of base salary. Northwind contributes 6 percent of salary to the company pension plan, matched to employee contributions up to that amount. Staff receive a yearly wellness allowance of 400 euros that can be spent on gym memberships, sports equipment, or mental health services. A lunch benefit card is loaded with 11 euros per working day. Employees who cycle to work can lease an electric bicycle through the company bike scheme, with payments deducted from gross salary.

Learning and career development. Each employee has an individual learning budget of 1,500 euros per year for courses, conferences, and certifications. Unused budget does not roll over. Internal mentoring is organised through the Compass programme, which pairs new hires with a mentor from a different department for their first nine months. Promotions between levels are decided twice a year by a calibration committee, in October and in April. Engineers can choose between a management track and an individual contributor track after reaching level L4. We run an internal conference called Northwind Days every September, where teams present demos and lessons learned. Attendance is voluntary but strongly encouraged.

Travel and expenses. Business travel must be booked through the corporate travel tool at least 14 days before departure where possible. Economy class is the default for flights shorter than six hours; premium economy is allowed for longer flights. The daily meal allowance while travelling is 45 euros domestically and 60 euros abroad. Expense reports must be submitted within 30 days of the trip with scanned receipts attached. Taxi rides are reimbursed only when public transport is unavailable or after 21:00. Travel to customer sites for robot installations is coordinated by the Field Operations team, which also arranges safety equipment and site access badges in advance.

Security and IT. All laptops use full-disk encryption and must be locked when unattended. Passwords must be at least 14 characters long, and multi-factor authentication is mandatory for email, source code, and the HR portal. Company data may not be stored on personal cloud accounts. Suspected phishing emails should be reported with the Report button in the mail client, which forwards them to the security team. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the IT service desk within one hour by calling extension 4400. Visitors to any site must be registered in advance and must wear a visitor badge at all times. Access to the firmware signing keys is limited to four named release managers.

Product overview: Hauler H2. The Hauler H2 is our mid-size autonomous mobile robot for warehouse picking and pallet transport. It carries a maximum payload of 600 kilograms and travels at up to 2.0 metres per second on flat floors. The H2 uses a 48-volt lithium iron phosphate battery that delivers about 10 hours of continuous operation and recharges to 80 percent in 50 minutes at a docking station. Navigation relies on two lidar sensors and a downward-facing camera that reads floor fiducial markers. The chassis is rated IP54 against dust and water splashes. The H2 is certified to the ISO 3691-4 safety standard for driverless industrial trucks.

Product overview: Hauler H5. The Hauler H5 is the heavy-duty model designed for cold storage and manufacturing plants. It can lift loads of up to 1,500 kilograms and operates in temperatures as low as minus 30 degrees Celsius thanks to a heated battery compartment. Top speed is limited to 1.5 metres per second when loaded. The H5 adds a 3D time-of-flight camera for detecting overhanging obstacles such as forklift tines. Its swappable battery pack can be exchanged in under three minutes, allowing round-the-clock operation. Customers usually deploy the H5 alongside the smaller H2 fleet, managed from the same fleet software.

Fleet software: Beacon. Beacon is the fleet management platform that coordinates all Hauler robots on a site. It assigns missions, plans traffic to avoid congestion at intersections, and schedules charging so that no more than 20 percent of the fleet charges at the same time. Beacon integrates with warehouse management systems through a REST API and supports webhooks for mission events. Site maps are created by driving a robot manually around the facility once in mapping mode. Beacon runs on an on-premise server, and a cloud dashboard provides read-only analytics. Software updates are released every six weeks and are staged to one robot first before the rest of the fleet.

Support and maintenance. Customers with a standard support contract can reach the support desk from 07:00 to 19:00 central European time on weekdays. Premium contracts include 24/7 phone support and a guaranteed on-site response within 8 hours for critical failures. Preventive maintenance is recommended every 2,000 operating hours and includes replacing drive wheel treads and cleaning lidar windows. Error code E-217 indicates a blocked safety scanner and is usually resolved by cleaning the scanner cover. Error code E-340 means the battery management system detected a cell imbalance, and the robot must be taken out of service until a technician inspects it. Spare parts are shipped from the central warehouse in Tampere.

Sustainability and ethics. Northwind aims to be carbon neutral in its own operations by 2030. All three sites run on certified renewable electricity, and robot batteries are collected at end of life through a take-back programme with a recycling partner. Suppliers must sign the Northwind supplier code of conduct, which prohibits forced labour and requires conflict-free sourcing of minerals. Employees can raise concerns anonymously through the Speak Up channel, which is operated by an independent third party. Retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith is a dismissible offence. Our annual sustainability report is published every May on the company website.
